title: Founders in focus: Amjad Masad of Replit
summary: Replit CEO Amjad Masad shares how the AI platform empowers teams to build software, partner with Okta on SSO, and secure autonomous AI agents.
body_markdown:
Each month we highlight one of the founders of an[Okta Ventures](https://www.okta.com/company/okta-ventures/) portfolio company. You’ll learn more about them and how they work with Okta. This month, we’re speaking with Amjad Masad, Co-Founder and CEO of Replit.


## What is Replit and what is your mission?


[Replit](https://replit.com/) is an AI platform that helps people build software and put AI agents to work. Our mission is to make building software as accessible to someone with an idea as it is to someone who knows how to code.


Students were among the first to build apps on Replit. Then people began using it to run their businesses. We have users from 85% of the Fortune 500 building with Replit.


As more people build at work, the opportunity goes beyond creating an app. A team can build a tool to solve a problem it knows well, then put an agent to work on the routine tasks that tool makes possible. That’s what we mean by a Self-Driving Company: People decide what matters and where approval is needed, while agents take on more of the day-to-day work.


## What were you doing prior to Replit that led you to this moment?


I grew up in Jordan, where my father introduced me to computers at an early age. By 10, I was writing simple apps to solve algebra problems. At 13, I sold an app to the owner of an internet cafe and used the money to take my entire class to McDonald’s.


That experience gave me the confidence to keep building. Years later, another app I built caught the attention of a company in the US. I moved there in 2012, worked at Codecademy, and later joined Facebook. In 2016, Haya Odeh and I started Replit to give more people the opportunity that building software had given me.


## What is Replit’s solution? What challenge does it solve?


Replit brings building, collaborating, and deploying software into one place. You can describe an idea in your own words, work with an AI agent to build it, and get it into people’s hands without having to piece together tools, infrastructure, and services yourself.


For businesses, that means more people can build without giving up control over who can access company systems or approve changes before they go live. Role-based access controls, isolated environments, and audit logs help teams manage access, limit risk, and see what happened.


As agents take on more of the routine work, people stay in charge of what to build and whether it’s ready to use. For experienced developers, that means less time on repetitive coding and more time on the decisions that make a product useful.


## Why did Replit want to work with Okta?


Making software easier to build is only part of the job. Our vision is a Self-Driving Company, where people decide what needs to happen and AI agents take on more of the day-to-day work. For that to work, teams need to know who authorized an agent to act, what it can access, and when a person needs to sign off.


That’s why we wanted to work with Okta. As a leader in identity and security and a Replit customer, Okta brings both technical expertise and firsthand experience using our tools. We were glad to welcome Okta Ventures as an investor in our most recent funding round.


## How is Replit working with Okta? What support do you look for in a corporate partner?


Okta is both a Replit customer and a technology partner, and Okta Ventures is an investor. One practical example of the partnership is single sign-on (SSO). Replit supports SAML SSO with Okta, so employees can use their existing work accounts to access Replit, and IT can manage that access the same way it does for other company tools.


We look for more than capital in a corporate partner. Because Okta uses Replit, their teams can give us feedback grounded in their own experience. Okta also brings a different perspective through their work in enterprise identity: They understand what IT teams need before they can confidently give people access to a new tool. We also look for opportunities to reach customers together when doing so solves a problem for them.


We want someone with an idea to be able to build it, and their IT team to feel confident saying yes.


## What trends do you expect to see in the AI and software development industry?


AI is changing how companies work on a scale few technologies have matched. The shift is from software that suggests a next step to agents that can carry it out. Replit calls this vision a Self-Driving Company: People set priorities and stay accountable for the results, while agents take on more of the day-to-day work.


That requires an environment the company controls. Replit calls it an Agent Habitat: a place where agents can use company tools and information within clear limits. The company decides what an agent can access, what it can do on its own, and when a person needs to sign off.


Human judgment matters more, not less. An agent can build an application, but people still decide whether it solves the right problem and whether it’s ready to use.
